audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL consensus mechanisms (PoW difficulty adjustment, Clique PoA), contract deployment validation (EIP-3541), historical data pruning (EIP-4444), and wallet chain switching (EIP-2015). All specifications directly interact with EL components including block validation, transaction processing, EVM execution, and P2P networking.

in_scope: Clique PoA consensus validation and signer voting (EIP-225)
Historical data retention and P2P serving (EIP-4444)
Wallet RPC interface for chain switching (EIP-2015)

misclassified_entities.rationale: This entity is part of the internal system - it's the node's own signing component for Clique PoA. It's not external data crossing a boundary, but rather an internal operational component of the EL client itself.
misclassified_entities.recommended_action: Remove from external entities or reclassify as internal component

misclassified_entities.rationale: In the context where it appears (voting mechanism subgraph), this represents the current node itself proposing votes. This is internal state transition, not external input. The actual external threat is malicious blocks from peer nodes, not the voting action itself.
misclassified_entities.recommended_action: Remove from external entities - the threat comes from peer-delivered blocks with votes, not from an abstract 'authorized signer'

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network (devp2p)
data_flows: Block headers with difficulty values and Clique signatures
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are completely untrusted. Any node can join the network and propagate data. All received blocks, transactions, and data must be cryptographically validated. Malicious peers could send invalid difficulty values, forged Clique signatures, malformed blocks, or request DoS attacks through historical data queries.
security_controls_required: ECDSA signature verification for Clique blocks
Difficulty calculation validation against parent block
Block timestamp validation
Signer authorization verification against current signer set
Signing limit enforcement (prevent spam from malicious signers)
Historical data age verification before serving (HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS)
Rate limiting on P2P requests

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer/Miner via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners/block producers are external entities attempting to produce valid blocks. They are untrusted because they could attempt to submit blocks with incorrect difficulty values (bypassing difficulty bomb), invalid timestamps, or other consensus violations to gain unfair mining advantage.
security_controls_required: Difficulty validation using fake block number calculation post-fork (EIP-4345)
Proof-of-work verification
Block timestamp validation
Fork activation block detection

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
data_flows: Runtime bytecode returned from init code execution
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit contract deployment transactions. Deployers are completely untrusted and could attempt to deploy malicious code. EIP-3541 specifically addresses the threat of deploying bytecode starting with 0xEF which would conflict with future EOF format, breaking forward compatibility.
security_controls_required: First-byte validation of returned runtime code (reject 0xEF)
Exceptional abort on validation failure (consume all gas)
Validation applies to CREATE, CREATE2 opcodes and direct deployment transactions

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator Providing Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SEMI_TRUSTED because the node operator is running the client and has privileged access, but checkpoint data must still be validated. A compromised or malicious checkpoint could lead to syncing to an invalid chain state (long-range attack). While there's a trust relationship, the checkpoint itself requires cryptographic validation against known network state.
security_controls_required: Checkpoint validation against known state roots
Time-bound validation (checkpoint must be recent within weak subjectivity period)
Cross-validation with multiple sources when possible
Checkpoint age verification (must not exceed HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS)

trusted_external_entities.name: External Historical Data Provider (IPFS, Portal Network, Indexers)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Out-of-band data retrieval (IPFS, Portal Network, The Graph, torrents)
data_flows: Historical block headers older than 1 year
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External data providers are completely untrusted third parties. They could serve falsified historical data to compromise applications relying on historical blockchain state. While EIP-4444 enables data pruning, it creates a dependency on untrusted external sources for historical data verification.
security_controls_required: Cryptographic validation against known state roots
Block hash verification against canonical chain
Receipt proof validation
State proof verification where available
Multi-source verification when possible

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via JSON-RPC
data_flows: Chain switch requests with chainId and RPC URLs
Historical data queries for old blocks/receipts
RPC endpoint URLs provided by dApp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Decentralized applications interact with wallets and nodes via JSON-RPC. They are completely untrusted as any website can act as a dApp. Malicious dApps could attempt SSRF attacks via crafted RPC URLs, phishing attacks with fake chain parameters, or DoS attacks through excessive historical data queries.
security_controls_required: RPC URL sanitization (block localhost, private IPs)
Chain parameter validation against known chain list
User confirmation prompts for chain switches
SSRF prevention in RPC URL validation
Rate limiting on historical data queries
Phishing detection for chain name/parameter mismatches

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote RPC Endpoint Provided by dApp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP/HTTPS connection to external RPC server
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote RPC endpoints provided by dApps are completely untrusted. They could be malicious servers designed to return fake chain data, perform man-in-the-middle attacks, or serve as phishing infrastructure. The wallet must validate responses before trusting the endpoint.
security_controls_required: HTTPS enforcement for RPC connections
ChainId verification (must match claimed chain)
Response validation and timeout handling
Certificate validation for HTTPS connections
No automatic trust of returned data

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via UI Interaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet user interface (approval dialogs, chain management)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SEMI_TRUSTED because the user owns the wallet and should control its behavior, but users can be socially engineered. Users may unknowingly approve malicious chain switches or provide compromised checkpoints if deceived by phishing attacks. The wallet must provide clear security warnings and validation to protect users from their own mistakes.
security_controls_required: Clear security warnings for unknown chains
Visual distinction between trusted and untrusted chains
Parameter validation even after user approval
Phishing detection warnings
Preventing approval of obviously malicious configurations (localhost RPC, etc.)

boundary_edges.description: Peer node sends Clique PoA block via P2P network for validation
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted block data crosses network boundary - must validate ECDSA signature, signer authorization, signing limits, timestamp, and extraData format

boundary_edges.description: External user submits contract creation transaction with init code
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted bytecode crosses transaction boundary - must validate returned runtime code does not start with 0xEF to prevent EOF format conflicts

boundary_edges.description: Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint for initial sync
boundary_edges.security_implication: Semi-trusted checkpoint data crosses operational boundary - must validate checkpoint authenticity and age to prevent long-range attacks

boundary_edges.description: Peer transmits block data via devp2p network protocol
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted block data from P2P network - must validate before storage and track age for pruning

boundary_edges.description: Peer requests historical block data via devp2p
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted data request could be DoS attack - must validate requested data age and enforce HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS limit

boundary_edges.description: dApp requests historical data older than retention window
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted application making data request - must be handled through external data providers with validation

boundary_edges.description: External provider returns historical blockchain data
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted historical data from third party - must cryptographically validate against known state roots before use

boundary_edges.description: dApp calls wallet_updateEthereumChain to request chain switch
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted dApp request crosses JSON-RPC boundary - must validate chainId format, sanitize RPC URLs, and require user approval

boundary_edges.description: Malicious dApp sends crafted chain switch request
boundary_edges.security_implication: Attack vector for SSRF and phishing - must detect and block internal URLs, validate against known chain list, warn user

boundary_edges.description: Peer sends block requiring difficulty bomb validation
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted block with difficulty claim - must recalculate expected difficulty using fake block number offset post-fork

boundary_edges.description: Miner produces block for difficulty validation
boundary_edges.security_implication: Untrusted miner could claim incorrect difficulty - must validate difficulty calculation matches expected value with bomb delay

notes: All valid external entities have associated boundary edges.
Two entities (EXT-LOCAL-SIGNER, EXT-AUTHORIZED-SIGNER) were identified as misclassified internal components.
EXT-PEER-NODE appears in multiple contexts (block propagation, historical data requests) - consolidated as EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P.
EXT-DAPP appears in multiple contexts (historical queries, chain switching, malicious attacks) - consolidated as EXT-DAPP-USER-REQUEST.
User entity (EXT-USER renamed to EXT-WALLET-USER-INPUT) represents semi-trusted human input requiring security warnings.
All entities represent genuine external data sources crossing system boundaries into the Execution Layer.
